verdict.rationale: Smithery's docs say each published server gets a dedicated server page where users can "discover, try, and install" the MCP, which implies a browser-based way to try a server before integrating, but nothing describes it as a tool inspector or playground. The only documented way to actually call tools ad hoc is the CLI (`smithery tool call`), which is not browser-based. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented browser inspector/playground UI, evidence of invoking individual tools with custom arguments and viewing responses in the browser, and hands-on or independent corroboration.
